standard.title: Connections between language and cultural practices
standard.description: identify connections between the target language and cultural practices
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have noticed that language reflects cultural practices and that the target language is spoken across diverse communities (AC9LS2U04). They can notice connections. They have not yet used analytical vocabulary to discuss these connections or reflected on cross-cultural comparisons systematically.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify and explain connections between the target language and cultural practices — using conceptual vocabulary and reflecting on similarities, differences and their own cultural position.

nodes.label: Using conceptual vocabulary for language-culture analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use conceptual terms to discuss connections between target language and cultural practices — explaining the connection, not only naming it.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two conceptual terms (identity, behaviour, celebration, belief) in a discussion about a target language language-culture connection — explaining the connection.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss cultural practices using terms like identity, behaviour, celebrations, beliefs; respond to discussion prompts about cultural meaning; explore how language features carry cultural values (e.g. naming conventions, forms of address, affective expressions); identify words that reflect cultural priorities.
wider: Research a target language cultural practice and explain the language associated with it — using at least three conceptual terms
Identify a culturally specific target language expression and explain what value or belief it encodes — providing an English equivalent or explaining why one does not exist
nodes.hinge_reason: Conceptual vocabulary for discussing language and culture is the analytical tool for all subsequent cultural reflection. Students who can only describe cultural practices without the conceptual frame cannot engage with the increasingly analytical cultural work from subsequent bands.

response_modes.reason: Using conceptual vocabulary requires students to move from description to analysis. Structured discussion prompts with conceptual vocabulary scaffold this analytical move.

success_criteria: Uses at least two conceptual terms when discussing a target language language-culture connection
Explains at least one connection between a target language feature and a cultural practice — not only identifies it

nodes.label: Cross-cultural comparison and personal reflection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare cultural practices across target language communities and their own context, reflecting on feelings of familiarity and difference.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one cultural practice in the target language that feels familiar and one that feels different from their own, with language evidence for each.
nodes.typical_width: Compare communicative conventions across target language communities and their own context; reflect on language use with different audiences; explore First Nations Australian cultural expressions and compare with target language community expressions; notice how language reflects cultural values in texts.
wider: Explore representations used in cultural expressions of First Nations Australians and find parallel patterns of cultural expression in target language communities

Reflect on a moment where target language cultural conventions felt different — describe the language, the behaviour and their reaction, and explain what the difference reveals about each culture's values

response_modes.reason: Cross-cultural comparison develops through encountering varied cultural domains. Each domain reveals different aspects of the language-culture relationship.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Personal cultural reflection — noticing one's own reactions to cultural difference — is the beginning of genuine intercultural competence. Students who can articulate this are developing the self-awareness that makes them effective cross-cultural communicators.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one culturally familiar and one culturally different practice, with language evidence for each
Reflects on their own cultural position in at least one comparison — not only describing the other culture
